title: Seems like a great idea, but in actual usage it is not.
text:
Seems like a great idea, but in actual usage it is not.. See, here's the thing, I would love it if the splatter screen itself wasn't so easily damaged. I have used this twice, once making burgers on a cast iron skillet over medium heat and I got those white blistery things on it that so many have mentioned. I used it again on a non-stick skillet over low heat and there was no additional damage.

Problem is though, that you need the splatter screen far more for things that, you know, actually splatter, which will often mean food with more fat, at a higher than low heat. So now it basically just sits there, doing nothing but looking all mopey and damaged, and I end up using an old fashioned metal screen splatter screen, which lets way more splatter out. If these guys could just make the material a little tougher, this would be amazing. But they haven't and it's not.
